image_prompt.text: The central town the whole map radiates out from — clustered houses with a castle at its heart and marked entrances where the guards stand.
A market stall for the merchant set at the town centre, so trading sits in one tight cluster rather than scattered through the streets.
The castle keep in the town and the dragon's mountain peak, both tall enough to be picked out from anywhere on the map and used to orient by.
Worn roads threading out of the central town and connecting every area — forest, mountain, mystical zone and waterside — into one route network.

Eight small blocky pixel-art figures, each 2-3 studs tall, standing on the terrain: a red-orange warrior by the town, a purple-blue mage in the mystical zone, a green archer in the forest, brown-tan villagers by the houses, a gold merchant at the market stall, silver-grey guards at the town entrances, a gold crowned king in the castle, and a dark red dragon on the mountain peak.
A mountain rising at one edge of the map with the land stepping up toward it, its peak the highest ground and the dragon's perch.
A river running across the map into a lake, cut into the terrain as a real feature rather than a painted texture.
A forest zone of densely packed trees covering one region of the map, with the archer standing among them.
A mystical, magical zone picked out by glowing effects, where the mage stands.

layout_placement.text: The ground each of the eight figures occupies: warrior at the town edge, mage in the mystical zone, archer in the forest, villagers by the houses, merchant at the market stall, guards on the town entrances, king in the castle, dragon on the mountain peak.

notes: Genres: the prompt self-declares 'top-down RPG adventure map', so both are named. RPG leads — the town, castle, king and dragon are its content — and owns the shape; Adventure contributes path-trail for the paths connecting all areas.

SET: the space is fully built but nothing is described as walking through it — the figures are 2-3 studs tall (well under avatar height), the map is a 32-unit grid, and it is specified as viewed from a slight isometric angle so the characters read. Treated as a diorama the camera looks at. This was the closest call in the run; if a player avatar is meant to walk the paths, drop SET and traversal checks come back.

Preset caveat: MMO Town Hub taken on its own shape (world-single), with teleporter-link dropped — the prompt asks for paths connecting the areas, not fast travel, and travel plinths were never requested.
The town is carried by safezone-town rather than the universal settlement-density row, to avoid emitting the same settlement twice.
CHECK is from water-body only, and should clear: a river and lake on a single-surface top-down map, with no swimming volume and nothing self-occluding.
No P3: houses, shops and the castle are described from outside only and nothing is entered, so they are facades.
terrain-relief is tiered rather than P2 — the mountain rises, but no caves, tunnels or overhangs are asked for.

The prompt's configurable attributes have nowhere to live in this handoff: CharacterScale (default 1), TerrainDetail (1-3), MapSize (grid 32). NumberOfCharacters (8) is carried as the count on npc-population.

would have asked: Sounds like a single continuous overworld built around a town hub — a central town of houses with a castle, a market cluster, roads out to every area, and the castle and mountain peak as landmarks you can orient by, plus the eight characters, the forest, the mountain, the glowing mystical zone and the river or lake. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?
would have asked: confirming this is one continuous map rather than separate zones, since the paths connect all areas — that keeps it on the proven single-pass build.
would have asked: whether anyone actually walks this map, or whether it is a display map viewed from the isometric angle. I read it as a display map and routed SET.
would have asked: ColorTheme is offered as 'Medieval' or 'Fantasy' but never chosen — which one should the map be built in?
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
